text: Sigrid Ingeborg Henriette Wienecke née Stadfeldt (March 13, 1819 – April 18, 1907) was a Norwegian-Danish composer who produced over 140 psalms and musical pieces. She was born in Frederikshald, Norway, to Asgeir Johnson Stadfeldt (1786–1831) and Anna Bruun Tordenskjold (1781–1848). After her father's death, she moved to Oslo with her mother. In 1834, she married Friedrich Ferdinand Wienecke (1809–1877), a singing teacher employed by the Christiania Theater; the couple had one daughter who died in infancy. Wienecke aspired to become an actress, but her husband deemed it unsuitable for someone of her social class; she nonetheless took piano lessons. The family moved to Copenhagen in 1839, where both Friedrich and Henriette unsuccessfully sought employment at the Royal Theater. In 1840, she settled permanently in Copenhagen with her mother and husband. In 1848, following the death of her mother, she retired from social life, underwent a religious conversion, and began composing psalms and songs based on texts by Hans Christian Andersen and others. She and her husband became followers of N.F.S. Grundtvig and Nicolai Gottlieb Blædel (1816–1879), and hosted bible studies and religious concerts in their home. She died in Gentofte, Denmark.
